These small calculations make the arithmetic behind a chapter's design
judgment inspectable. They use selected, already published observations and
write new result directories. The five detailed studies and the nominal
OTA examples retain their own frozen inputs, measurements and reproduction.

## Reference-current investment

Chapter 3 asks what A37→A75 gains by increasing the reference from two units
to five while retaining the signal and output-load devices. The calculation
checks the exact circuit inventory, drawn area, finite resistors and historical
role-variance table, then distinguishes the cost, predicted SD and original
confirmation's MAE decision.

Download [reference-investment.py](reference-investment.py), the
[expected summary](reference-investment-summary.json),
[three-case table](reference-investment.csv) and
[file manifest](manifest.json). The script requires standard Python 3.9 or
later, with no external Python package or SPICE run. Original calculation
code is MIT-licensed; the site's [license notices](../../licenses/LICENSE.md)
and the source package retain applicable text/data and third-party terms.

Use a new directory:

~~~bash
mkdir reference-investment-example
cd reference-investment-example
curl --fail --location https://ds54e.github.io/analog-design-notes/learn/calculations/reference-investment.py --output reference-investment.py
curl --fail --location https://ds54e.github.io/analog-design-notes/downloads/gain-study-v1.0.zip --output gain-study-v1.0.zip
python3 -I reference-investment.py --source-zip gain-study-v1.0.zip --output results-001
~~~

The program checks the ZIP against SHA256
`4d2dda32baa15f173c6a897e7429ba0e421b0fa1738ff722fe8b889d1cf3e55f`
and checks its eleven selected members. It independently counts MOS units
and area from the SPICE bodies and configuration, verifies unchanged units
and resistors, and cross-checks the original two contrast representations.
`results-001` contains `reference-investment-summary.json` and
`reference-investment.csv`; an existing destination is refused.

Expected results include +37.489 µA positive-delivered current and +1.44 µm²
of drawn MOS area. The original predicted total SD changes from 78.657 to
72.369 mV. Inverse reference-count scaling estimates 72.367 mV for the latter.
Removing only A37's reference variance leaves 67.851 mV: that row is a
restricted mathematical floor, with no finite current/area assigned. It is
not a third fabricated circuit or a newly simulated result.

The source budget remains the original native-Jacobian source-transfer
estimate. This calculation does not recalibrate it, rerun the reference maps,
refit a distribution or acquire new confirmation. It preserves the two
original 464-pair MAE reductions and intervals; predicted SD and observed
MAE are different quantities. The original data and ZIP remain unchanged.

The [first-study reproduction](../../studies/gain-operating-point-accuracy/reproduce.qmd)
provides its graph/statistics regeneration and selected saved-physical native
OP/AC replay. The [initial-OTA example](../../studies/learning-common-mode-v1/reproduce.qmd)
separately covers its two exposed common-mode conditions. Neither native
route is required by this arithmetic-only exercise.

The isolated-mode check on 2026-09-13 retrieved the original ZIP anonymously
into a clean directory. Standard Python regenerated both result files with
exact bytes. It installed no Python package and ran no native simulator. This
is a same-host reproduction check, not an independent scientific replication.
